items.title: Periodic incompressible Newtonian idealization
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Adopted three-dimensional, incompressible, constant-density and constant-viscosity Newtonian continuum model on a flat periodic cell, with zero body force and no temperature field. Its weak realization uses the unforced periodic Leray–Hopf class. It asserts no empirical universality, global smoothness, or uniqueness.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds. Fix $L>0$ as the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, so the physical side length is $L\,\mathrm m$, and use the flat periodic cell $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ with normalized spatial measure $L^{-3}dx$. Spatial coordinates in physical volume integrals are measured in metres. Assume Countable Choice for the stated Fourier and Sobolev space conventions. The velocity is a vector field $u:I\times\mathbb T_L^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with SI units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the mass density is a constant primitive parameter $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$; the dynamic viscosity is a constant primitive parameter $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$; and the mechanical pressure $p$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The body-force density is zero (its SI unit is $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$), and there is no temperature variable in this model.

For classical fields take $u\in C^1(I;C^2(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C^1(I;C^1(\mathbb T_L^3))$. Adopt incompressibility $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and the local momentum balance
$$\rho_0\bigl(\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D(u),\qquad D(u)=\tfrac12\bigl(\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}\bigr).$$
Here $\sigma$ is the Cauchy stress, so its traction on an oriented surface with unit normal $n$ is $\sigma n$; $D(u)$ is the symmetric rate-of-deformation tensor; and $\nabla$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Every term in the momentum balance has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Since $\operatorname{div}u=0$, this equation is equivalently
$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nu=\mu/\rho_0>0,\qquad \pi=p/\rho_0.$$
where kinematic viscosity $\nu$ and kinematic pressure $\pi$ have units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, respectively. All fields are periodic in each spatial coordinate; this is an ideal cell, not a wall-bounded vessel.

For the weak regime, use the global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf class. The spaces are $H$, the real $L^2$ vector fields whose divergence vanishes distributionally on $\mathbb T_L^3$, with unrestricted constant Fourier mode, and $V=H\cap H^1$, where $H^1$ consists of fields and first weak derivatives in $L^2$; use normalized spatial norms. Here $C_w([0,\infty);H)$ means that $t\mapsto (u(t),h)_H$ is continuous for every fixed $h\in H$; the time-dependent $L^p$ spaces are the corresponding Bochner spaces. A weak velocity has $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\rm loc}(0,\infty;V)$, strongly attains $u_0\in H$ as $t\downarrow0$, and satisfies, for every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field $\phi$ compactly supported in time,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0.
$$
The tensor pairing is $L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i\,dx$, and the gradient pairing is $L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i\,dx$. The class also requires
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\qquad(t\ge0),
$$
and a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2\qquad(s\in S\cup\{0\},\ t\ge s).
$$
This weak convention asserts neither uniqueness nor pressure regularity. These equations and the solution class are adopted model assumptions; they are not deductions that every physical fluid obeys them.

references.title: Lenya Ryzhik, Lecture Notes for Math 256B, Version 2024
references.locator: §1.3, printed pp. 9–11, especially the symmetric velocity gradient, Newtonian stress, and incompressible reduction.

references.title: Luigi C. Berselli and Stefano Spirito, On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations, Fluids 6(1), 42 (2021)
references.locator: §1, printed pp. 1–3, for the constant-density, constant-temperature incompressible model, zero force, and periodic domain.

items.title: Weak continuation of the adopted periodic viscous model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $L>0$ be the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, with physical side length $L\,\mathrm m$; let $\rho_0>0$ be constant in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $\mu>0$ constant in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$. Set $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$. On $\mathbb T_L^3$, use normalized Lebesgue measure $L^{-3}dx$, and let $H$ be the real $L^2$ vector fields whose divergence vanishes distributionally, with unrestricted mean mode, and $V=H\cap H^1$, where $H^1$ consists of fields and first weak derivatives in $L^2$. Here $H^s_\sigma$ means the real Fourier-weighted Sobolev space with weights $(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s$, Fourier divergence condition $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$ for $k\ne0$, and unrestricted constant mode. Let $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity measured in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume Countable Choice. Then the adopted unforced periodic model has a global weak velocity $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V)$, where $C_w$ means continuity of each fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are strongly measurable Bochner spaces, with $u(0)=u_0$ and strong $H$ trace at zero. For every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field $\phi$ compactly supported in time it satisfies
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0,
$$
where the spatial pairings use the normalized measure and $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$. It also satisfies, for every $t\ge0$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,
$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
In SI units the kinetic energy is $K(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_{[0,L]^3}|u(t,x)|^2dx$, and the inequality implies
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le K(0).
$$
There is also a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_s^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(\tau,x)|^2dx\,d\tau\le K(s).
$$
This is a conditional model deduction about velocity; it asserts no pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, or empirical validity.

items.physical_scope: Conditional global weak velocity existence for the three-dimensional constant-density, constant-viscosity, unforced incompressible Newtonian model on a flat periodic cell. No pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, temperature evolution, or empirical universality is claimed.

items.title: Bounded no-slip Newtonian vessel model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Adopted constant-density, positive-viscosity, zero-force incompressible Newtonian continuum on a fixed nonempty bounded open three-dimensional vessel. No-slip is the H_0^1 solenoidal-closure condition; no pointwise trace is asserted on an arbitrary open boundary. The weak result concerns velocity only, and makes no universal empirical or thermal claim.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a fixed nonempty bounded open vessel in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres. Assume Countable Choice for the stated Sobolev space conventions. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, where divergence is the distributional divergence (equal to the classical divergence for these smooth fields), $H$ as its closure in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $V$ as its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$; here $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields in the $H^1$ norm, and $H^1$ uses square-integrable fields and first weak derivatives. The adopted no-slip condition means $u(t)\in V$, not a pointwise boundary value. This closure convention does not identify $V$ with every divergence-free member of $H_0^1$ on an arbitrary open set and does not assert a boundary trace theorem.

Take a constant mass density $ho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, a constant dynamic viscosity $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and zero body-force density in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. For classical fields $u\in C^1(I;C^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C^1(I;C^1(\Omega))$, adopt $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the Cauchy stress $\sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D(u)$ with $D(u)=	frac12(
abla u+(
abla u)^{\mathsf T})$, and the local balance $ho_0(\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u))=\operatorname{div}\sigma$ in the interior. The velocity has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, pressure and stress have units $\mathrm{Pa}$, spatial derivatives have units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and $
u=\mu/ho_0$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. No temperature field is included.

For the weak regime, take $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{m loc}(0,\infty;V)$, with $u(0)=u_0\in H$ and strong $H$ trace at zero; $u_0$ is an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Here $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing, and each time-dependent Bochner space uses strongly measurable maps with the indicated norm, locally on every finite interval. Interpret this model through the solenoidal variational identity: for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)	o V$,
$$

Here all spatial pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure on $\Omega$, $(u\otimes u):

items.title: Global weak velocity in the no-slip vessel model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be any nonempty bounded open set in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, let $H$ be its $L^2(\Omega)$ closure, and let $V$ be its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported smooth fields and $H^1$ has the norm formed from the $L^2$ norms of a field and its first weak derivatives. Let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$, and $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Then the adopted unforced no-slip model has
$$
u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V),
$$
where $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are Bochner spaces of strongly measurable maps, with $u(0)=u_0$, strong $H$ trace at zero, and, for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
It satisfies the initial energy inequality
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\qquad(t\ge0),
$$
and a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
Here spatial norms and pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure, $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$, and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. Thus the SI kinetic energy $E(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2dx$ obeys
$$
E(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_\Omega|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le E(0).
$$
The no-slip condition is only the stated $H_0^1$ closure condition; the result supplies no pressure or pointwise wall trace.

items.physical_scope: Conditional global weak velocity for a constant-density, positive- viscosity, zero-force incompressible Newtonian model on any fixed bounded open three-dimensional vessel. No pointwise boundary trace, pressure regularity, uniqueness, smoothness, thermal evolution, or empirical universality is claimed.

items.title: Weak rectangular Newtonian velocity and pressure
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i)\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a finite open rectangle in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres, with $a_i<b_i$, and write $U=(0,\infty)\times\Omega\subset\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $(t,x_1,x_2,x_3)$. For an open $O\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, set $\mathcal D(O)=C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb C)$ and, for each compact $K\subset O$, set $\mathcal D_K(O)=\{\psi\in\mathcal D(O):\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq K\}$ with Fréchet seminorms $p_m(\psi)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in K}|\partial^\alpha\psi(x)|$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$. Give $\mathcal D(O)$ its locally convex LF topology, the finest locally convex topology making every inclusion $\mathcal D_K(O)\to\mathcal D(O)$ continuous; real and finite-dimensional vector test-function spaces carry the corresponding real and componentwise topologies. Let $\mathcal D'(O)$ be the vector space of continuous complex-linear functionals on $\mathcal D(O)$, with bilinear pairing $\langle F,\psi\rangle=F(\psi)$; a spacetime distribution on $U$ is an element of $\mathcal D'(U)$. A locally integrable field $f$ is identified componentwise with the distribution $\psi\mapsto\int_U f\psi\,dt\,dx$. For $F\in\mathcal D'(O)$ and a multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, define $\langle\partial^\alpha F,\psi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\langle F,\partial^\alpha\psi\rangle$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D(O)$. Derivatives of vector or matrix distributions are taken componentwise; for scalar $F\in\mathcal D'(U)$, $\nabla_xF=(\partial_{x_i}F)_{i=1}^3$, for a matrix distribution $A$, $(\operatorname{div}A)_i=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}A_{ij}$ for $i=1,2,3$, and $\Delta$ acts componentwise as $\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2$.

Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, where for smooth fields $\operatorname{div}a=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x_i}a_i$, let $H$ be its closure in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and let $V$ be its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields and $H^1$ uses square-integrable fields and first weak derivatives. This convention does not identify $V$ with all divergence-free members of $H_0^1$ on an arbitrary open set and makes no pointwise trace assertion. Let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$, and $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume AC and Countable Choice. In addition, assume the following rectangular test-divergence inverse: for $D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):\int_\Omega h=0\}$ with its subspace LF topology, a continuous linear map $R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with the componentwise LF topology satisfies $\operatorname{div}(Rh)=h$; for each compact input support there is one compact output support, and every fixed-support restriction is continuous for the test-function seminorms above.

Then there are a weak velocity $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V)$ and a real kinematic-pressure distribution $\pi\in\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning it takes real values on real-valued tests, with units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$. Here $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing, and the time-dependent spaces use strongly measurable Bochner maps on finite intervals. The velocity has $u(0)=u_0$ and strong $H$ trace at zero, and for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$ it satisfies
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
All spatial pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure, with $(u\otimes u)_{ij}=u_i u_j$, $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$, and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. For every $t\ge0$ it satisfies
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,
$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
Fix one real scalar test function $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$. The following spacetime equation is an equality in $\mathcal D'(U)^3$ under the stated distributional-derivative convention, and this fixed normalization is
$$
\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,
$$
$$
\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0
$$
for every $a\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$. Such a $\theta$ exists because a product of normalized smooth compactly supported interval bumps belongs to $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and has integral one. The physical pressure distribution $p=\rho_0\pi$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, is unique under this fixed scaled normalization, and satisfies
$$
\rho_0\partial_tu+\rho_0\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)+\nabla p=\mu\Delta u
$$
as a spacetime distribution. The SI kinetic energy $E(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2dx$ obeys $E(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_\Omega|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le E(0)$. This conditional result asserts no pressure in $L^2$, corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction.

items.physical_scope: Conditional no-slip weak velocity and normalized distribution pressure on a finite rectangular vessel, with constant density, positive constant viscosity, and zero force. Pressure is only a spacetime distribution; no L2 estimate, corner regularity, or pointwise wall traction is claimed.

items.title: Thermal balance requires an additional coupling
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
The periodic mechanical model has a velocity field and a kinetic-energy inequality with viscous dissipation, but it has no temperature variable. The separate thermal model uses a fixed rectangle $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with lengths $L_i>0$ in metres, an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ measured in seconds, and a temperature field $T:\overline\Omega\times I\to\mathcal T\subset(0,\infty)$, where $\mathcal T$ is an open interval, measured in kelvins; its time derivative through order one and spatial derivatives through order two extend continuously to $\overline\Omega\times I$. In that thermal supplier, $u\in C^1(\mathcal T,\mathbb R)$ is the internal-energy density in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $c(T):=u'(T)>0$ is the volumetric heat capacity in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$; write $e_{\mathrm{th}}:=u$ to distinguish this caloric function from the mechanical velocity notation. The thermal flux is $j_Q:\overline\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; in the adopted local-energy postulate it and its first spatial derivatives extend continuously to $\overline\Omega\times[t_0,t_1]$ for every compact $[t_0,t_1]\subset I$, and $j_Q\cdot n=0$ on every face, where $n$ is the outward unit normal. Its local balance is $\partial_t e_{\mathrm{th}}(T)+\operatorname{div}j_Q=0$, with $\operatorname{div}j_Q=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x_i}(j_Q)_i$. The Fourier constitutive assumption is $j_Q=-K(x,T)\nabla T$, where $\nabla T=(\partial_{x_i}T)_{i=1}^3$, $K:\overline\Omega\times\mathcal T\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ has entries in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, and $K_s:=(K+K^{\mathsf T})/2$ satisfies $z^{\mathsf T}K_s(x,T)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^3$. The separate entropy-production theorem and constant-conductivity Neumann heat-evolution theorem retain their own regularity and initial-data conditions.

Neither branch identifies any part of the mechanical viscous dissipation with a source in the thermal balance, and the two branches use different domains. A coupled temperature evolution therefore requires an additional model assumption specifying the conversion of mechanical energy into heat and a common domain/field interface; it does not follow from the weak periodic continuation or from the thermal entropy and heat-evolution results.
